title: Why he quit: the Depression and a dollar a night
summary: Eddie says he quit around 1929 because of the Depression, when bands got a dollar a piece for nights lasting from 8 until morning.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: The Depression years and the WPA band

blocks.x: I quit acting. Quit all of getting in the 40s. I mean, quit all of them. You didn't even play occasionally after the 1940s? No. I didn't go around them. I didn't visit them. I didn't do nothing. I stick to my son. I got mad. I raised my family. So I quit playing music. Now if somebody come hired me. I'll go to help them. If not to work with me.
I'll be in. Boxing Sparks faster. Actually, I quit in 29. Why?
Why? No. Why did you quit? Well, I'm going to tell you why. Things were bad. The depression was in 29, from 29 to 32. The band that played around together, they paid for a dollar a night.
A dollar a piece. A dollar a piece?
And from 8 to the people leave. Sometimes 6, sometimes 5, sometimes 7 in the morning. You get ready to knock off a couple walking you had to save. So they need one dollar.
